entries.title: Long XLE on a crude one-day thrust in the 5 to 6 percent band
entries.cell: energy price-state
entries.trigger: RE-ARMED 2026-09-02 after the old arm FIRED IN FULL and the cell died anyway. What happened: USO popped +5.460% into the [5,6)% band at 1.65 ATR with PPI (+5 td) and CPI (+6 td) both outside a three-session hold, so every stated leg cleared, and the parked numbers reproduced to the decimal (38 episodes, +1.251% mean, excess +1.105pp, 73.7% hit, sign p 0.0025). It died on four independent grounds. (1) THE ATR LEG IS A FILTER THAT DOES NOT FILTER: >=1.50 ATR moves the excess from +1.105pp to +1.121pp, 1.6 basis points, while discarding 22 of 38 episodes whose own excess is +1.094pp. The condition that made this an arm rather than a state removes 58% of the sample and separates nothing. (2) DEFINITION FRAGILITY: the bucket ladder is an interior spike with [4,5) at -0.186pp and [6,7) at +0.499pp, and sliding the lower edge to 4.8% halves the result to +0.685pp. A per-session decomposition puts 76% of the three-day number on day three, with day four giving back -0.774%, so h=3 is a one-day spike rather than a hold. (3) CONCENTRATION: top three of sixteen armed episodes are 72% of the total, drop-best-3 leaves +0.292pp, and the only recent era is wrong-signed (2026 armed -0.451% on n=2, band -1.217% on n=4). (4) THE BETA RESIDUAL SURVIVES THE BAND: re-estimated crude beta 0.506 (t 57.7), armed residual +0.506pp at a 62.5% hit and sign p 0.227, band residual +0.827pp at a 55.3% hit and sign p 0.314 - the registry's 2026-08-11 closure intact. TURNS ON only when the crude-beta residual clears on its own terms: sign p <= 0.10 at a hit rate above 65% on at least 20 band episodes, AND the [4,5)% bucket ceasing to be negative (-0.186pp today), so the band is a shelf rather than a spike. The ATR leg is RETIRED from the arm; do not re-add it without fresh attribution. Two findings that do NOT need re-testing: an NFP inside the hold is NOT the CPI/PPI containment effect (+1.973% on n=7 against +1.088% on n=31, Welch t +0.64), and the CPI/PPI exclusion IS real (-0.550% in against +1.985% out, Welch t -2.51). Standing book overlap, verified again: 47 Overbot Vol Spike SHORT signals on USO >= +5% days at avgR +0.286, and on armed trigger days 9 of 10 energy positions the book held across the hold were SHORT at avgR +1.046. Dial max on any armed episode 80.9 against today's 87.5.

entries.title: Long TLT with the whole investment-grade complex pinned at 52w lows
entries.cell: rates price-state
entries.trigger: THE JOIN MUST BE SHOWN TO FILTER RATHER THAN RE-ANCHOR. The old arm (tight rung fires as the FIRST trigger day in >= 10 td) FIRED IN FULL on 2026-09-10 -- TLT, IEF and LQD all closed EXACTLY at their trailing-252 lows with the previous trigger 16 td back -- and the cell died anyway, so re-arming on the same price state would only re-run the same kill. What happened: the parked arithmetic reproduced to the digit under declusters(10) (N=18, +0.385pp excess, 83.3% hit, sign p 0.0038, 15.1x cost), concentration was excellent (top-2 episodes 9% of total), LOYO was positive throughout (+0.42 to +0.51pp), the vehicle was TLT-specific (rank 1 of 5) and the dose trap did NOT fire (+87.0 bp of 252-session yield thrust is the 45th percentile of the eleven episode doses, response flat; TLT within 0.05% of the low pays +0.605% on N=7 at 85.7% against +0.155% for merely near). It died on a decomposition nobody here had run: matching each PARENT anchor to its cell counterpart inside 21 td, the anchors the join DELETES pay -0.256% (N=6) and the ones it KEEPS measured at the parent's own date pay -0.213% (N=10), while those same ten episodes measured at the cell's LATER date pay +0.470%. Filtering is worth +0.016pp and RE-ANCHORING +0.683pp of a +0.699pp total; six of eleven anchors move 1-17 td forward for an average +1.139pp. The IEF leg deletes ZERO episodes while moving the mean +0.314pp. Two confirmations: the excess rises MONOTONICALLY with the decluster gap (+0.048pp at gap 1, from a parent worth nothing at N=76 / 57.9% / sign p 0.1034, to +0.733pp at gap 63), which is a selector rather than a state; and bucketing the freshness claim by offset from the episode start into SIX bins instead of two makes it oscillate in sign three times (0 +0.470%, 1-2 -0.210%, 3-5 +0.224%, 6-10 +0.169%, 11-21 -0.315%, 22+ +0.352%) with the STALEST bucket paying nearly as much as offset 0. TURNS ON when the parent anchors the join DELETES underperform the ones it KEEPS by >= 0.35pp, both measured at the PARENT's own anchor dates, over >= 12 parent anchors; today that gap is +0.043pp. Equivalently the decluster-then-filter ordering (the version with no date shift in it) must reach sign p <= 0.05 in its own right; it is currently N=4, +0.330%, 3-1, p 0.3125. ONE NUMBER ARGUES THE OTHER WAY and is recorded rather than buried: against a null that re-anchors the parent by a random draw from the join's OWN shift distribution, the cell's +0.470% has P = 0.0223, so the join does pick better dates than a blind delay. TWO RECONCILIATIONS OWED before this is ever scored again: (a) the arm's prose ('first trigger day in >= 10 td', a MASK) and the parked statistic (declusters(trig,10), which restarts at the last KEPT day) describe DIFFERENT populations -- 11 anchors against 19, differing by 8 dates; the mask form is the executable one. (b) The anchor-swap-free version (TLT & LQD only) pays +0.139pp = 4.6x cost, under the 5x bar. Also on file: ZERO of the ten historical episodes ever entered on a CPI session, and the edge is one bar wide (h=1 +0.453pp, h=2 +0.017pp at a 50% hit, h=3 +0.475pp, h=5 +0.067pp). Do NOT rediscover: carrying the parent's anchors forward a flat 4 sessions pays +0.329% at 87.5% on N=16, sign p 0.0021 -- better than the cell, with no IG legs at all -- but +6 td pays -0.505%, so the delay ladder is noise.

The full ladder is non-monotone and peaks exactly at the pitched value ([1.25,1.5) +0.058%, >=1.5% +0.638%, >=1.75% +0.507%, >=2.0% +0.267%). SECOND debt, independent of the first: the mechanism has to start when the trade does.
